title: The Window I Almost Left Open
scene: A chilly morning at home, when a small sound interrupts the rush to leave.
sceneJa: 肌寒い朝、家を出ようとした瞬間に風の音が聞こえる。窓を閉め忘れていたことに気づき、慌てずに確かめる。

chunks.en: I was halfway out the door,
chunks.ja: 玄関から出かけかけたとき、
台所で何かがカタカタ鳴る音が。
窓を開けっぱなしにしていたことに。

chunks.en: I was tempted to ignore it,
chunks.ja: そのままにしようかと思ったが、

chunks.en: but the wind was picking up,
chunks.ja: 風が強くなってきていたので、
カーテンが風にあおられていた、
鍵も念のため確かめて、

chunks.en: By the time I reached the stairs,
I'd stopped worrying about the window,
chunks.ja: 窓のことは気にならなくなったが、

chunks.en: and started wondering about the stove.
chunks.ja: 今度はコンロが気になり始めた。

questions.question: Which split keeps the expression together?
options: It took / me a second to / figure out
It took me a second / to figure out / I'd left the window open.
It / took me / a second to figure
questions.explanation: It took me a second is a natural unit meaning I needed a brief moment.

questions.question: What does 'double-checked the lock' mean?
options: Locked it twice with two keys.
Checked again to make sure it was locked.
Asked someone else to lock it.
questions.explanation: Double-check means verify again, not necessarily do the action twice.

questions.question: Why does the narrator mention the stove at the end?
options: To show another small worry replacing the first.
To explain why the window was open.
To say they are cooking breakfast.
questions.explanation: The ending gently jokes about how one worry can turn into another.

speak: In 30 seconds, describe a small thing you almost forgot before leaving home. Say what made you notice it, what you checked, and how you felt afterward.
review: New: It took me a second（気づくまで少し時間がかかった）, Sure enough（案の定）, double-check（念のため再確認する）. Review: I was tempted to（〜したくなった）, By the time（〜するころには）.
